newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kirch takes majority stake in German TV network.
newsitem.headline: Kirch takes majority stake in German TV network.

text.p: German media mogul Leo Kirch, taking advantage of a new law on television ownership rights, has raised his stake in the German television network SAT 1 to 59 percent, a magazine reported on Saturday.

Germany's Focus magazine said Kirch bought on January 2 an additional 16 percent stake in the Mainz-based private television network, a day after a new German law allowed for individual companies to hold a majority stake in a network.

Kirch, who owns one of the largest media empires in the world, purchased a 15 percent stake in SAT 1 from AV Euromedia and a one percent stake from Ravensburger Film + TV GmbH. Kirch had previously owned 43 percent of SAT 1.
Terms of the deal, which must now be approved by officials in the German state of Rheinland-Pfalz, were not disclosed. A Kirch spokesman was also unavailable on Saturday for comment.
The Axel Springer Verlag publishing group, of which Kirch holds a 35 percent stake, currently owns 40 percent of SAT 1, while publisher Eberhard Ebner holds a one-percent stake.

Kirch, who began his empire in 1958 with the purchase of Fellini's La Strada film for $56,000, controls a media group spanning Europe that includes the rights to more than 15,000 feature films and 50,000 hours of telvision programming.
